key_prerequisites.name: Two-Digit by One-Digit Multiplication Using Area Models

sections.normalized_html: How many feet are in [MATH: 14] yards?
sections.readable_text: How many feet are in [MATH: 14] yards?

sections.normalized_html:
We start with the unit conversion between yards and feet:

[MATH: 1\, \textrm{yard} =3 \, \textrm{feet}]

We want to figure out how many feet are in [MATH: {\color{blue}{14}}] yards. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}{14}}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: 14 × 1yard = 14 × 3feet; 14yards = 14 × 3feet]

We can calculate [MATH: 14\times 3] using an area model:

According to our model,

[MATH: 14\times 3 = 30+12 = 42.]

Therefore, [MATH: 14] yards equals [MATH: 42] feet.

items.title: Converting Lengths From Feet to Inches

key_prerequisites.name: Two-Digit by Two-Digit Multiplication Using Area Models

sections.normalized_html:
We start with the unit conversion between feet and inches:

[MATH: 1 \,\textrm{ft} = 12 \,\textrm{in}]

We want to figure out how many inches are in [MATH: 45] feet. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 45\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: 45 × 1ft|= 45 × 12in; 45ft|= 45 × 12in]

We can calculate [MATH: 45 \times 12] using an area model:

According to our model, [MATH: 45 \times 12 = 400+50+80+10=540.]

Therefore, [MATH: 45 \, \textrm{ft}] equals [MATH: 540 \, \textrm{in}.]

Item 2 — Example: Converting Lengths From Yards to Feet

We can calculate [MATH: 14\times 3] using an area model:
